nodes.label: Migration 0002 prediction_result_matches_status
nodes.rationale: Makes predictions result columns nullable and adds the CHECK tying them to prediction_status.

nodes.label: Prediction And Assessment Endpoints
nodes.rationale: POST runs resolve-snapshot, call ML, evaluate rules, generate recommendations, persist and return. Snapshot resolution order: supplied id validated against the project, else latest, else a new one. 503 if the ML service is unreachable with nothing persisted; 422 if it returns no delay estimate. No PATCH or DELETE, because editing a prediction would destroy the only basis on which a past decision can be reviewed.

nodes.label: The Prediction Flow
nodes.rationale: Authorize, read live project data, freeze a project_feature_snapshots row, POST it to the ML service, persist prediction plus explanations plus recommendations, render, and later record the real outcome joined to the snapshot only at training time. Freezing the snapshot is what makes the rendered prediction defensible months later.

nodes.label: actual_outcomes Table
nodes.rationale: The ML target in its own table, UNIQUE on feature_snapshot_id so there is one label per snapshot, carrying the composite FK and the temporal guard.

nodes.label: Composite Foreign Keys Against Cross-Project Contamination
nodes.norm_label: composite foreign keys against cross-project contamination
nodes.rationale: (feature_snapshot_id, project_id) on both predictions and actual_outcomes makes linking a snapshot outside its own project unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.

nodes.label: Data Leakage Prevention
nodes.rationale: Target leakage is the most common way an ML project produces excellent offline metrics and useless real-world predictions, so the schema defends in four independent ways: physical separation, a documented column boundary, elapsed-time features treated as inputs, and a temporal guard trigger.

nodes.label: predictions Table
nodes.rationale: Records an inference attempt. Composite FK (feature_snapshot_id, project_id) makes cross-project attachment structurally impossible, and ON DELETE RESTRICT prevents deleting a snapshot a prediction depends on so the audit trail cannot be silently broken.

nodes.label: predictions_result_matches_status Constraint
nodes.rationale: SUCCESS requires both predicted_delay_days and risk_level; FAILED and PENDING require both NULL. Written as a CASE over the status rather than a chain of ORs, because a CASE with no ELSE returns NULL and a NULL CHECK passes - so a newly added fourth status would slip past unvalidated. Forcing a future author to touch this constraint is the point. risk_level is included because writing 'LOW' would be the same fabrication one column over.

nodes.label: trg_actual_outcomes_temporal_guard
nodes.rationale: Rejects any outcome whose outcome_date precedes the snapshot_date it labels. A CHECK constraint cannot express this because it spans two tables, so labelling an old snapshot with an earlier observation becomes a database error rather than a silent modelling bug.

nodes.label: Never Compare Two Wall-Clock Readings
nodes.rationale: NOW() returns the transaction timestamp and PGlite's clock has millisecond resolution, so two fast statements can share a tick. The updated_at tests backdate the row with the trigger disabled and assert the trigger moved it forward - deterministic and a stricter test besides.

nodes.label: Schema Idempotency Test
nodes.rationale: The single most valuable test in the file: schema.sql is pasted by hand into the SQL Editor and a half-applied run gets pasted again. An earlier version declared the RLS helper functions before public.profiles existed and failed on first apply - that class of bug is what this catches.

nodes.label: SET ROLE Is Required For RLS Tests
nodes.norm_label: set role is required for rls tests
nodes.rationale: PGlite connects as a superuser and PostgreSQL exempts superusers and table owners from RLS entirely, so a policy test that forgot to switch role would pass unconditionally while proving nothing. Every assertion runs through actingAs / actingAsAnon in helpers/identity.ts.

nodes.label: Failed Inference Still Writes A Row
nodes.norm_label: failed inference still writes a row
nodes.rationale: When the ML call fails, a predictions row is written with status FAILED and NULL results so the failure is visible and countable but no number is invented. The snapshot is kept and can be re-scored once the service recovers. The UI must therefore render three states - prediction, in progress, unavailable - since one that assumes a number will show a failed inference as a healthy project.

nodes.label: Stateless ML Service
nodes.rationale: The FastAPI service receives a feature vector and returns numbers; it holds no database credentials and never writes to Postgres. Statelessness means the model can be retrained, redeployed or rolled back without touching application data, and a failure there degrades prediction only.

nodes.label: Documented Snapshot Column Boundary
nodes.rationale: schema.sql carries a header listing what must never be added (delay_days_target, actual delay, actual completion date, realised cost overrun); verified automatically by a naming-pattern audit, with actual_delay_days existing in actual_outcomes and nowhere else.

nodes.label: Migration 0002 Deliberately Does Not Rewrite Rows
nodes.norm_label: migration 0002 deliberately does not rewrite rows
nodes.rationale: It cannot distinguish a fabricated 0 from a genuine 0-day forecast filed under the wrong status, so it aborts and documents the query for finding and clearing them by hand.

nodes.label: Physical Feature/Label Separation
nodes.rationale: Features live in project_feature_snapshots and the label in actual_outcomes, so a training query must perform an explicit, reviewable JOIN and a careless SELECT * over the feature table cannot pull the label in by accident.

nodes.label: ML Service Leakage Boundary
nodes.rationale: The service never queries a database - it holds no credentials and receives the snapshot in the request body, so it cannot reach actual_outcomes even in principle. FeatureSnapshot uses extra='forbid' so a payload carrying actual_delay_days is rejected with 422 at the edge rather than quietly ignored. Training applies the same boundary: audit_dataset.py classifies seven columns as leakage and train.py refuses to run if any reaches the feature matrix.

nodes.label: Environment-Sourced Credentials
nodes.rationale: SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and JWT_SECRET are required; ML_SERVICE_URL and ALLOWED_ORIGINS optional. Nothing is hardcoded and .env is gitignored; the service-role key is server-side only.

nodes.label: GET /health
nodes.rationale: Returns 200 whenever the process is serving; database state is reported in services.database.status (ok, schema_missing, unreachable), not in the HTTP status. Implemented in src/services/health.service.ts.

nodes.label: Migration 0003 auto_provision_profiles
nodes.rationale: on_auth_user_created trigger provisions a VIEWER profile for every new auth user and backfills existing users.

nodes.label: PGlite Test Engine
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL compiled to WebAssembly: same planner, constraint machinery and SQLSTATE codes. Chosen because almost everything asserted is enforced by the database - a hand-written mock would accept SQL that PostgreSQL rejects, so a suite built on one would pass while proving nothing. Bundles PG16 while Supabase runs 15+.

nodes.label: Bearer JWT Authentication
nodes.rationale: Identity from the JWT sub claim, authority from public.profiles.role read server-side. ES256 via JWKS for this project with HS256 legacy support; algorithm pinned and iss, aud, exp and a UUID sub all asserted. A 503 rather than 401 means the backend could not determine how to verify tokens.

nodes.label: API Role Permission Matrix
nodes.rationale: ADMIN full; ANALYST and VIEWER read nationally; OFFICER reads and writes assigned projects only. 'Assigned' means an explicit project_assignments row or having created the project, mirroring is_assigned_to_project() in the schema.

nodes.label: Authorization Middleware Modules
nodes.rationale: auth.middleware.ts (requireAuth), authorize.middleware.ts (requireRole, requireProjectAccess/Read/Write) and authorization.service.ts (canAccessProject, isAssignedToProject, mirroring is_assigned_to_project() in the schema), with config/roles.ts holding the role constants so no controller re-derives a policy decision and the earlier case mismatch cannot recur.

nodes.label: Credential Boundary Table
nodes.rationale: Anon key: frontend and backend. Service-role key and JWT_SECRET: backend only, never the frontend. The ML service holds no Supabase credentials and no database connection at all.

nodes.label: Express Backend Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: The only component that talks to both the database and the ML service: verifies the JWT, resolves role from profiles, enforces authorization, validates with Zod, builds feature snapshots, orchestrates the ML call and persists results, and never returns credentials, raw SQL errors or stack traces.

nodes.label: React Frontend
nodes.rationale: Holds the Supabase anon key and the user's JWT and never the service-role key; shipping that key to a browser would hand any visitor full read/write access to every project. The anon key is safe to expose precisely because RLS constrains it.

nodes.label: Health And Observability
nodes.rationale: GET /health returns 200 whenever the process is serving with database state in the body; the probe is a single-row, single-column read of projects bounded by 2s and deliberately avoids head:true, because with head the client discards the response body and a 'table not found' error is indistinguishable from success.

nodes.label: Live API Verification (Phase 3)
nodes.rationale: backend/tests/live/api.live.test.ts exercises all 27 endpoints over real HTTP with real ES256 sessions - 61 tests, excluded from npm test, gated on LIVE_E2E=1, with every fixture removed in afterAll. It carries the weight because every service queries through supabaseAdmin and bypasses RLS, so requireProjectAccess has no backstop.

nodes.label: Live Database Verification (Phase 2.3)
nodes.rationale: backend/scripts/verify-live-db.ts runs 52 behavioural checks against the deployed schema. Behaviour rather than catalog introspection, partly because PostgREST exposes only the public schema and partly because a row in pg_policies proves a policy was created, not that it does anything. RLS evidence comes only from publishable-key clients with real ES256 sessions. Indexes and NUMERIC serialisation are explicitly out of scope.

nodes.label: Dual Supabase Key Generations
nodes.rationale: Both new (sb_publishable_ / sb_secret_) and legacy key formats are accepted with fallbacks so a project can migrate without a coordinated deploy; key format and variable name are independent, and migrating formats changes nothing about trust.

nodes.label: Supabase PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Stores application and historical data and enforces its own invariants; RLS protects the direct-from-client path, Supabase Auth owns auth.users and profiles extends it with application role.

nodes.label: Pre-Production Checklist
nodes.rationale: Define the VIEWER/ANALYST visibility boundary, confirm the OFFICER-narrower-than-VIEWER asymmetry is intended, add the signup profile trigger, audit every service-role route, and re-test the policy matrix against real Supabase Auth JWTs.

nodes.label: profiles Table
nodes.rationale: 1:1 with auth.users, carries role (ADMIN/OFFICER/ANALYST/VIEWER, default VIEWER) plus department and state. Role is never accepted from a client; profiles_update_own_no_role_change blocks self-promotion by comparing the new row against the stored role.

nodes.label: Row Level Security Model
nodes.rationale: Enabled on all 14 tables with 42 default-deny policies. OFFICER is scoped to assignments because a field officer's authority is project-specific; ANALYST and VIEWER are read-only oversight roles; snapshots, predictions and outcomes have no OFFICER update policy because they are the audit trail; model_versions is readable by all and writable only by ADMIN because the registry decides which model serves traffic.

nodes.label: Build Phase Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Phases 1-5 done (backend foundation, database schema/RLS, business APIs, FastAPI ML service, prediction orchestration); Phase 6 (dashboard APIs, LLM summaries, deployment) not started.

nodes.label: Express + TypeScript Backend
nodes.rationale: Node.js / Express 4 / TypeScript 5 / Supabase / Zod / Axios / JWT. Implements the product flow PREDICT to EXPLAIN to PRIORITIZE to ACT.

nodes.label: Database Regression Suite
nodes.rationale: Automated checks that schema.sql, seed.sql and migrations behave the way docs/DATABASE.md says they do; each file builds its own database so suites run in parallel and a failure cannot cascade.

nodes.label: Phase 3 Business API Reference
nodes.rationale: Base path /api, JSON responses; only endpoints that exist are documented - unimplemented LLM summaries and SHAP explanations have no routes.

nodes.label: LandGuard AI System Architecture
nodes.rationale: Four components - React frontend, Express backend, Supabase PostgreSQL, FastAPI ML service - implementing the flow PREDICT to EXPLAIN to PRIORITIZE to ACT.

nodes.label: Database Design
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 15+ on Supabase; 14 tables, 42 RLS policies, 47 indexes. Four principles: normalized not one wide table, the database enforces its own invariants, the ML audit trail is immutable, and features and labels are physically separate.

nodes.label: LandGuard AI
nodes.rationale: Decision-support system for Indian infrastructure projects: tracks land acquisition, compensation, legal disputes and operational risk, and turns that record into early warnings about projects likely to slip.

nodes.label: Fail-Fast Environment Validation
nodes.rationale: The server refuses to start if any required environment variable is missing or malformed; it prints the offending fields and exits with code 1, so misconfiguration surfaces at boot rather than as a runtime fault.

nodes.label: Liveness Independent Of Database Health
nodes.rationale: Restarting the API because Postgres blipped turns a database incident into an API outage, and a health endpoint that goes dark is useless when you most need it. The probe reads one column of one row from projects under a 2s timeout so the endpoint cannot hang.

nodes.label: What The Database Suite Does Not Cover
nodes.norm_label: what the database suite does not cover
nodes.rationale: Real Supabase Auth JWTs (auth.uid() is shimmed), the backend authorization layer (the Node backend uses the service role key and bypasses RLS), and performance (indexes are asserted to exist, not to be used).

nodes.label: Supabase Auth Shim In The Harness
nodes.norm_label: supabase auth shim in the harness
nodes.rationale: tests/helpers/db.ts supplies auth.users, auth.uid(), the authenticated/anon roles and Supabase GRANTs. The shim lives in the harness and never in schema.sql so the file under test stays byte-for-byte the file pasted into the Supabase SQL Editor; auth.uid() reads a session setting so RLS tests can switch identity.

nodes.label: created_by Rejected From Input
nodes.rationale: created_by is set from the authenticated caller and rejected if supplied, because authorship grants project access - accepting it from input would let a caller hand access to someone else.

nodes.label: Amounts And Areas Are Strings
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL NUMERIC is exact decimal and an IEEE-754 double cannot hold every value, so callers send strings, receive strings and must not parse them to Number for arithmetic.

nodes.label: VIEWER Profile Provisioning On Signup
nodes.rationale: A profiles row is created by the on_auth_user_created trigger with role VIEWER as a hard-coded literal, never from signup metadata. An authenticated user with no profile row gets 403, not a default role.

nodes.label: 400 vs 422 Distinction
nodes.rationale: 400 means 'this is not shaped like a request'; 422 means 'this is a valid request the domain refuses' - land acquired exceeding land required, or project data too incomplete for a snapshot. 409 covers duplicate codes and existing 1:1 records; 503 a dependency outage. Raw database text is never returned.

nodes.label: The 22P02 Malformed-UUID Bug
nodes.rationale: GET /api/projects/not-a-uuid returned 503 because translateDbError had no case for SQLSTATE 22P02 and fell through to 'database unavailable' - wrong twice, reporting a nonexistent outage and inviting a retry that can never succeed. The in-memory fake returned null for unknown ids so no unit test could reach the path. Fixed at two layers: requireProjectAccess rejects malformed ids with 400, and translateDbError maps 22P02/22007/22003 to 400.

nodes.label: The Persistent-Session Anonymous Client Trap
nodes.rationale: A reported RLS leak was really a test bug: supabase-js keeps a session on the client instance even with persistSession: false and the same object had signed test users in. The tell was that 'anonymous' saw exactly one profile row - what a VIEWER sees. The script now proves current_app_role() is NULL before drawing conclusions, because a test that fails in the direction of 'looks like a security hole' is the worst way to be wrong.

nodes.label: Explicit Authorization Failure Modes
nodes.rationale: No profile row is 403 and never a fallback to VIEWER, because under the prototype policy VIEWER reads every project nationally so defaulting to the least role would grant national read to any valid token holder. A lookup failure is 503, not 403 - a database outage is not an authorization decision.

nodes.label: Pinned JWKS Verification Mode
nodes.rationale: auto mode historically treated any JWKS failure as 'no JWKS' and fell back to HS256 - a downgrade attack, since a transient outage would move verification onto a possibly weak JWT_SECRET. The verifier now distinguishes published, definitively absent and indeterminate, failing closed on the third; algorithms are pinned per mode and the modes never share key material, foreclosing algorithm confusion.

nodes.label: Request Pipeline Ordering
nodes.rationale: requireAuth then requireProjectAccess then validate(zod) then controller then service. Authorization precedes validation so an unauthorised request is refused without the API first reporting whether its payload was well-formed, which would turn error messages into an oracle about an inaccessible project. Collection endpoints have no project id, so read scoping happens inside the service - a forgotten filter there would leak every project in the country.

nodes.label: SIH Prototype Role Visibility Policy
nodes.rationale: VIEWER and ANALYST read nationally as a documented prototype decision, because the brief does not define what bounds 'allowed project visibility' and guessing a boundary would hard-code it into the security model. It widens read for two already read-only roles, weakens no write protection, and is replaceable by narrowing SELECT policies using the existing profiles.state / profiles.department columns.

nodes.label: Deliberate Service-Role Client Usage
nodes.rationale: Used in exactly three places: profile.service.ts (resolving the caller's role before any authorization decision exists, otherwise a chicken-and-egg with the policy deciding whether they may read their own profile), authorization.service.ts (must see assignments the caller cannot), and business services. health.service.ts is the one service using the RLS-respecting client.

nodes.label: Two Enforcement Layers
nodes.rationale: RLS protects the direct client to PostgREST path but is bypassed entirely by the service-role key the backend uses; backend authorization covers API traffic only. Backend authorization is therefore mandatory, with RLS as the backstop if a handler forgets a check.

nodes.label: Money Precision (NUMERIC 18,2)
nodes.rationale: Exact decimal, never floating point: FLOAT cannot represent 0.10 exactly and accumulates error across sums, which is unacceptable for compensation figures. Rupees to paise; percentages NUMERIC(7,4); areas NUMERIC(14,4); day counts NUMERIC(10,2) because model output is continuous.

nodes.label: VIEWER/ANALYST National Scope Decision
nodes.rationale: The brief says 'read-only access according to allowed project visibility' without defining the bound - state, department or an explicit grant list each produce a different schema, and picking one now would hard-code a guess into the most expensive place to guess wrong. Replacement is contained: every affected policy is a SELECT policy containing the literal 'ANALYST','VIEWER', and profiles.state/department already exist to carry the boundary. The RLS tests assert the current scope so narrowing it fails loudly.

nodes.label: Normalized Schema, Not One Wide Table
nodes.norm_label: normalized schema, not one wide table
nodes.rationale: A wide table would force NULL-padding for every project missing a dimension, make constraints unenforceable, and turn every write into a lock on one hot row.

nodes.label: NUMERIC Arrives In JavaScript As A Number
nodes.norm_label: numeric arrives in javascript as a number
nodes.rationale: Corrected after live verification: PostgREST serialises NUMERIC as a JSON number, not a string. Values are correct but a JS double holds integers exactly only to 2^53 while NUMERIC(18,2) permits ~1e16, so the top of the range is not representable. Nothing is currently wrong because no code sums money in JS - derived values are generated columns copied through untouched - but aggregation must stay in SQL or go through a decimal library. Writes accept decimal strings, so the round trip is strings in, numbers out.

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER RLS Helper Functions
nodes.rationale: current_app_role(), is_admin() and is_assigned_to_project() read public.profiles, which is itself under RLS - without DEFINER the policy on profiles re-enters itself and recurses until PostgreSQL aborts, the single most common way a Supabase RLS setup breaks. search_path is pinned to public, pg_temp so they cannot be hijacked, and they are defined after the tables they read because a SQL function body is validated at CREATE time.

nodes.label: RLS Is Not Sufficient On Its Own
nodes.norm_label: rls is not sufficient on its own
nodes.rationale: The Node backend connects with the service role key, which bypasses RLS entirely, so every policy is invisible to backend queries. The backend must resolve role server-side, check assignment before OFFICER writes, reject non-ADMIN role changes, and reserve the service-role client for operations that genuinely need to bypass RLS.

nodes.label: ML Service API Key Requirement
nodes.rationale: All endpoints except /health require X-API-Key, and ENVIRONMENT=production without ML_SERVICE_API_KEY refuses to start - an unauthenticated ML endpoint on a network is an open risk-scoring oracle. /health stays open so an orchestrator can probe it.

nodes.label: Authorization Is Resolved Server-Side
nodes.rationale: The JWT proves who the caller is; public.profiles decides what they may do. Role is never read from the token because Supabase user_metadata is user-writable, so a correctly-signed token can carry any role its holder chose.

nodes.label: Three Non-Conflated Test Layers
nodes.rationale: Mocked (380 backend) and PGlite (179 database) suites prove logic; only the live suites (61 Supabase E2E, 12 ML integration, 64 live DB checks) prove the real project works. The layers are deliberately never conflated because a green mocked suite proves nothing about the deployed system.

nodes.label: The 21 Snapshot Features
nodes.rationale: Land, compensation, social scale, legal flags, risk-factor flags and elapsed time. Derived numerics are copied from the generated columns rather than recomputed in JavaScript to avoid float drift and disagreement with the source row; litigation_flag derives from court_cases_count so the two cannot disagree; notification_delay_days is null when the notification predates the planned start because a clamp to 0 would assert something the data does not say.

nodes.label: Feature Snapshot Endpoints
nodes.rationale: POST creates a snapshot with no request body - features are derived from current project data and the timestamp is the server clock, because backdating would corrupt the temporal integrity of the training set. A preview endpoint dry-runs the same computation and writes nothing.

nodes.label: Snapshot Immutability Enforcement
nodes.rationale: No updated_at column and no UPDATE trigger; no UPDATE policy for any role but ADMIN; ON DELETE RESTRICT on referencing FKs. Consequence: re-running a stored prediction against its stored snapshot reproduces the same input vector however far the live project has moved on.

nodes.label: real_case_studies.csv
nodes.rationale: 10 narrative case summaries from public reports, excluded from training by design not oversight: it has no delay_days_target, different columns and narrative text fields, so merging it would mean inventing a target.

nodes.label: data_quality Computed Not Stored
nodes.rationale: project_feature_snapshots has no provenance column and Phase 3 does not add one, so the data_quality block (issues, missingFeatures, sources, completeness) is returned for the caller to persist if needed.

nodes.label: Snapshot Immutability At Every Layer
nodes.rationale: No PATCH and no DELETE route exists, the service exposes no such method, and the database grants no UPDATE policy, has no updated_at column and restricts deletion of a referenced snapshot. Snapshots are never created as a side effect of editing project data, because auto-snapshotting would make 'which snapshot did this prediction use' meaningless.

nodes.label: Snapshot Refusal (422)
nodes.rationale: Creation is refused when the data cannot support an honest feature vector: no land record, missing required/acquired hectares, acquired > required, percentage outside 0-100, or a future date. Warnings (missing compensation, notification or planned start) are returned alongside a successful snapshot instead.

nodes.label: Elapsed-Time Features Are Inputs, Not Targets
nodes.norm_label: elapsed-time features are inputs, not targets
nodes.rationale: notification_delay_days and award_delay_days measure delay already observed as of snapshot_date between past events, so they are legitimate inputs - but must never be computed against a future or projected date.

nodes.label: The Feature Snapshot Concept
nodes.rationale: A project mutates continuously, so if predictions referenced live rows, reopening a prediction six months later would show today's values rather than the ones the model saw. For a system advising government officials, 'we cannot reconstruct why the model said 287 days' is not an acceptable answer, so project_feature_snapshots freezes the exact feature vector at prediction time.

nodes.label: Index Strategy
nodes.rationale: Explicit indexes added only where a real access path needs them; every index costs write throughput, so columns already covered by a UNIQUE constraint or by the leading column of a composite got none. Composite (project_id, snapshot_date DESC) and (project_id, created_at DESC) serve both plain lookup and the ordered 'latest' query.

nodes.label: Nothing Is Invented To Fill A Gap
nodes.norm_label: nothing is invented to fill a gap
nodes.rationale: A failed prediction stores NULL not 0; a missing feature is null not a substitute; a snapshot is refused rather than assembled from guesses. A fabricated zero is indistinguishable from a real measurement and gets learned as fact.

nodes.label: Risk Factors Endpoints
nodes.rationale: factor_type is a foreign key into risk_factor_types rather than a fixed enum, so new factor types are an INSERT not a schema change; an unknown code returns 422 pointing at GET /api/reference/risk-factor-types, which frontends should use to populate dropdowns rather than hard-coding a list that will go stale.

nodes.label: Migration Convention
nodes.rationale: Numbered, zero-padded, snake_case migration files after the baseline; applied via Supabase SQL Editor, supabase db push, or psql.

nodes.label: schema.sql As Canonical Baseline
nodes.rationale: schema.sql is the complete current schema and is deliberately not duplicated into migrations/ - one authoritative copy avoids the two drifting apart. A fresh install runs schema.sql alone; numbered files exist only for databases created before a change.

nodes.label: Applied Migrations Are Immutable
nodes.rationale: Once a migration has run on any shared environment it is never edited; it is fixed with a new migration. Migrations are idempotent where practical and wrapped in a transaction, except statements like CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY that cannot run inside one.

nodes.label: Adding A Risk Factor Type Is Not A Migration
nodes.norm_label: adding a risk factor type is not a migration
nodes.rationale: risk_factor_types is a reference table, so a new vocabulary entry is an INSERT rather than a schema change.

nodes.label: Assumptions And Deviations From The Brief
nodes.norm_label: assumptions and deviations from the brief
nodes.rationale: Recorded rather than silently invented: OFFICER sees fewer projects than VIEWER (implemented literally, flagged as unusual); national VIEWER/ANALYST read; generated columns cannot carry NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; predicted_delay_days is nullable under a CHECK; factor_type uses a lookup table; extra statuses added; migrations hold no copy of the baseline; demo predictions point at a placeholder model named demo-0.1.0-untrained with NULL metrics; profiles cannot be seeded in SQL because auth.users is Supabase-managed.

nodes.label: Why 0 Is The Worst Available Placeholder
nodes.norm_label: why 0 is the worst available placeholder
nodes.rationale: 0 is a valid, plausible 'no delay expected' reading, so a failure stored as 0 renders green on dashboards, drags AVG(predicted_delay_days) down so the more failures the healthier the portfolio looks, and is learned as fact by any training query that forgets to filter on status. A sentinel like -1 violates the >= 0 CHECK and must be remembered by every consumer forever. NULL is the only representation that means 'no value' to the database, to SQL aggregates and to every client library.

nodes.label: risk_factor_types Lookup Table
nodes.rationale: factor_type is a FK to a lookup table rather than a CHECK because the brief requires new factor types without destructive schema changes - adding one is a single INSERT rather than a constraint rebuild that revalidates the whole table. Closed lifecycle vocabularies (status, severity, role) stay CHECK constraints since they are not expected to grow.

nodes.label: The Database Enforces Its Own Invariants
nodes.norm_label: the database enforces its own invariants
nodes.rationale: Derived values are generated columns, vocabularies are CHECK constraints or lookup tables, cross-table relationships are composite FKs. A rule enforced only in the API holds for exactly one caller; a CHECK constraint holds for direct SQL, admin edits and every future service.

nodes.label: Feature Mapper
nodes.rationale: The inherited risk_rules.py reads 47 project fields while the deployed snapshot has 21 and exactly one name matches. The mismatch is a difference in kind, not naming: the rules want counts and percentages where the snapshot records booleans, and turning encroachment=true into unauthorized_occupation_cases=5 would be inventing a measurement. So app/services/feature_mapper.py maps 9 DIRECT and 11 DERIVED and marks 24 UNAVAILABLE; rules whose inputs are unavailable are skipped and reported, never evaluated against a guess.

nodes.label: Rule Engine
nodes.rationale: 15 rules across 13 categories (land progress, compensation, litigation, ownership disputes, land records, R&R, RoW, encroachment, forest clearance, possession, administrative delay, timeline, displacement scale). Every triggered rule returns its evidence - the field values that fired it - so a reader can check the finding rather than trust it.

nodes.label: FastAPI ML Service
nodes.rationale: Rule-based early-warning engine (primary) plus an experimental delay estimator (secondary) behind a FastAPI service the Node backend calls. Endpoints: /health (open), /predict, /evaluate-rules, /recommendations, /model-info, /feature-mapping.

nodes.label: ML Service Dependency Set
nodes.rationale: Deliberately small - every dependency is used and nothing is installed 'in case we need it later': fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic(+settings), pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, joblib, pytest, httpx.

nodes.label: assessment_complete Flag
nodes.rationale: assessment_complete: false means core inputs were missing, so a low risk_score reflects incomplete records as much as low risk; missing_inputs names what is absent and the result must not be presented as reassurance.

nodes.label: banded_rule Mutual Exclusivity
nodes.rationale: Severity bands within a rule are mutually exclusive so a project at 15% acquisition is penalised once, not once each for <75, <50 and <25 - enforced structurally by banded_rule rather than by discipline.

nodes.label: Risk Score Formula
nodes.rationale: 15 base plus the sum of contributions, capped at 95. The base reflects that an acquisition with nothing recorded is unassessed rather than risk-free; the cap leaves room for the unmeasured.

nodes.label: Assessment Sufficiency Check
nodes.rationale: Skipping rules deflates the score, so a project with nothing recorded would otherwise read as low-risk - the opposite of the truth. Raw rule coverage is a poor guard because 10 of 15 rules read NOT NULL booleans that evaluate happily against false and push coverage to 67%; an early version passed its sufficiency check on an entirely empty project for that reason. Sufficiency therefore also requires the core graded measurements, otherwise the response carries sufficient: false and missing_core_inputs.

nodes.label: Python 3.12 Pin
nodes.rationale: Not 3.14: the scientific stack's wheel availability on 3.14 was unverified at the time of writing, and debugging a source build is not a good use of a prototype's time.

nodes.label: Compensation Endpoint
nodes.rationale: 1:1 with project; compensation_pending and compensation_pending_percentage are database-calculated and supplying either returns 400. payment_status vocabulary NOT_STARTED / IN_PROGRESS / PARTIAL / COMPLETED / DISPUTED.

nodes.label: GET /api/projects/:projectId/full
nodes.rationale: Everything about one project in a single round trip; six reads run concurrently, one query per table regardless of child row count. Snapshots are summarised rather than returned in full, and summary counts live (OPEN / IN_PROGRESS) issues only because a resolved dispute is history, not current risk.

nodes.label: Land Acquisition Endpoint
nodes.rationale: 1:1 with project. Supplying land_acquisition_percentage returns 400 because the column is GENERATED ALWAYS STORED. Rules: acquired <= required, parcels acquired <= total, notification <= award <= possession, no negatives.

nodes.label: Legal Issues Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Many per project, addressed as (projectId, id); requesting one through a different project returns 404 - knowing its UUID is not enough to reach it. case_reference only when court_case is true.

nodes.label: Projects Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Paginated, filtered, role-scoped list plus create (ADMIN), read, patch and delete. DELETE cascades to child data but is refused with 409 if a prediction references one of its snapshots - the audit trail of what was predicted must not be erasable.

nodes.label: compensation Table
nodes.rationale: 1:1 with project; paid <= required enforced; last_updated maintained by its own trigger.

nodes.label: land_acquisition Table
nodes.rationale: 1:1 via UNIQUE project_id. land_award_after_notification and land_possession_after_award encode the statutory sequence notification to award to possession.

nodes.label: projects Table
nodes.rationale: Central entity with unique project_code, status CHECK, coordinate ranges and ordered date pairs. created_by uses ON DELETE SET NULL so removing a user never destroys project history, and actual_completion_date exists for record-keeping but is deliberately never copied into feature snapshots.

nodes.label: Generated Columns (GENERATED ALWAYS STORED)
nodes.rationale: land_acquisition_percentage, compensation_pending and compensation_pending_percentage. PostgreSQL recomputes on every write and rejects any INSERT/UPDATE targeting the column, so no client, future service, direct SQL session or dashboard admin can spoof a derived value - computing in Node would protect only the path that happens to go through Node. Division is guarded by CASE because a required total of 0 is legitimate. A generated column cannot declare NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, which is stricter than the brief, not weaker.

nodes.label: Migration 0004 prediction_assessment_fields
nodes.rationale: Adds combined-assessment fields on predictions, explanation_source on prediction_explanations and source_rule_id on recommendations.

nodes.label: prediction_explanations Table
nodes.rationale: Per-feature attribution with signed contribution scores, unique per (prediction_id, rank) and (prediction_id, feature_name).

nodes.label: Assessments Are Read Back, Never Recomputed
nodes.norm_label: assessments are read back, never recomputed
nodes.rationale: GET /assessment returns the stored prediction row, ranked explanations and recommendations; re-running the rules against today's data would answer a different question from the one the endpoint is asked. Explanations carry explanation_source RULE_ENGINE to keep rule contributions distinct from model self-attribution.

nodes.label: Deliberately Absent Routes
nodes.rationale: No SHAP explanations (explaining a model that loses to a median baseline would dress up noise as insight), no LLM summaries or dashboard analytics (Phase 6), and no API surface for actual_outcomes - which is part of why outcome data cannot reach a prediction.

nodes.label: Attribution Is Not Causal Proof
nodes.rationale: Contribution values describe how the model weighted a feature in producing its own output; a high score for title_issue_flag means the model leaned on it, not that the title issue provably caused the delay. UI copy and reports must not present them as proven cause.

nodes.label: shap Deliberately Not Installed
nodes.rationale: SHAP explains a model's contribution to its own output, so explaining a model that does not beat a median baseline would dress up noise as insight. The rule engine provides real, auditable explanations instead and is the primary signal by design.

nodes.label: combined5_land_acquisition.csv
nodes.rationale: 130 rows compiled from CAG audit reports - the ML training set.

nodes.label: neededfactors.csv
nodes.rationale: 50 rows, a feature-engineering draft and subset of the training set; reference only, not trained on.

nodes.label: ML Datasets And Provenance
nodes.rationale: Three files with declared origin and use; nothing in the pipeline reads the raw CSVs without going through scripts/audit_dataset.py first.

nodes.label: The Two Signals Are Never Merged
nodes.norm_label: the two signals are never merged
nodes.rationale: risk_assessment comes from the deterministic rule engine; predicted_delay_days is the historical median carrying no project-specific signal. There is no combined 'AI confidence' score and there will not be one - averaging a deterministic score with a figure that has no predictive content produces a number that looks authoritative and means nothing.

nodes.label: Honesty / Provenance Columns
nodes.rationale: record_status (REAL through REAL + IMPUTED PREDICTORS + PROXY TARGET), per-field imputation flags, and factor_imputed_count = 24 for every row including the four marked REAL. The headline is that all 22 predictor columns are imputed or derived for the entire dataset; only the target is real for most rows.

nodes.label: Categories Are Never Mixed
nodes.rationale: Verified project data, imputed values, demo data, rule-based warnings, ML estimates and actual outcomes are distinct things and are labelled as such.

nodes.label: model_versions Registry
nodes.rationale: A partial unique index allows at most one ACTIVE model so the serving model is unambiguous. mae, rmse and r2_score are NULLable on purpose - NULL means 'not yet measured' and a plausible-looking substitute is never written. r2_score is capped at 1 with no lower bound because R-squared is genuinely unbounded below.

nodes.label: Dataset Degeneracy (130 Rows, 22 Vectors)
nodes.rationale: 108 of 130 rows (83%) share one identical feature vector while their real delays span 12 to 2070 days, so for most of the data the model has no information to distinguish rows and the best any algorithm can do is emit the median. All 22 predictor columns are imputed or derived for every row. This is not a tuning failure and no hyperparameter search fixes it.

nodes.label: Grouped Cross-Validation
nodes.rationale: Ordinary K-fold puts copies of the same feature vector in both train and test, so a model that memorised 'this vector to the median of its training rows' scores well without generalising. GroupKFold over identical feature vectors prevents that; it makes the reported numbers worse, which is the point.

nodes.label: BASELINE_MEDIAN Prediction
nodes.rationale: No trained model beat a median baseline: median_baseline MAE 306.8 vs random_forest 323.6 and ridge 332.3, every R-squared negative, meaning the models explain less variance than a horizontal line. So the service reports the median, labels it BASELINE_MEDIAN, sets confidence LOW, and says in the response that it is not a model prediction.

nodes.label: xgboost / lightgbm Deliberately Not Installed
nodes.rationale: A gradient booster cannot extract signal the dataset does not contain; with 22 distinct feature vectors and 83% of rows sharing one it would memorise the 21 singletons and report a flattering in-sample R-squared that means nothing. scikit-learn's RandomForest already demonstrates that honestly at a fraction of the install weight.

nodes.label: The ML Claim Matches The Evidence
nodes.norm_label: the ml claim matches the evidence
nodes.rationale: No trained model beat a median baseline on 130 rows with 22 distinct feature vectors and every R-squared negative, so the rule engine is the primary signal and the delay figure ships labelled BASELINE_MEDIAN with confidence LOW.

nodes.label: expectSqlError Negative-Test Helper
nodes.rationale: Throws if the statement unexpectedly succeeds, so a guard that stops working fails loudly rather than passing quietly - a bare try/catch cannot tell those two apart.

nodes.label: Assert On SQLSTATE, Not Message Text
nodes.norm_label: assert on sqlstate, not message text
nodes.rationale: Error codes are stable across PostgreSQL versions and locales; messages are not. Where a specific constraint is the point of the test, err.constraint is asserted too.
